newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom seen worth 160-210 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom seen worth 160-210 bln Ffr.

text.p: Financial analysts value France Telecom at between 160 billion and 210 billion francs ($28-36 billion), a source close to the company said after consulting some 30 studies on the group.
This would make it the largest French company by market value and it would rank in the top 10 telecommunications companies in the world by market capitalisation.
Analysts published their studies this week following a March 20 company briefing ahead of an Initial Public Offering (IPO) of France Telecom shares.
The source said that indications of the price per share for the IPO were between 170 and 180 francs. A price range for the IPO will be announced on May 5.
It will be set by the Finance Ministry after advice from the independent Privatisation Commission. The state aims to raise between 30 and 50 billion francs from the sale of a minority stake.

It will be announced in the evening of Monday, May 5, after which France telecom chairman Michel Bon will leave on a roadshow to investors which will take him to almost all European capitals, the United States and Japan.

Not many analysts have gone public with their estimates, either out of legal considerations or to avoid upsetting the lead banks for the IPO - Banque Paribas and Banque Nationale de Paris - as it could reduce their chances of playing a role in the placement.
But of the few estimates which have appeared, French brokerage Oddo is the highest with 210 billion francs while French bank Societe Generale has 200 billion pencilled in.
At the lower end, ABN Amro Hoare Govett gave a range of 150 billion to 180 billion francs -- included in the overall range of estimates at its central value of 165 billion.

Credit Suisse First Boston issued a note which included a range of 169 billion and 195 billion francs. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell had no comment on reports its range was between 150 billion and 200 billion francs.
A Japanese bank in London put out a note saying that a price of 175 francs would make the company "very attractively priced."
"France Telecom compares very favourably with most of its European peers -- especially on the earnings, cash earnings and EBITDA multiples," the analyst wrote.
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation.

"While the prospective dividend yield is not as high as the other "mature" telco's, a prospective yield of 3.2 percent is above the average for the French market which currently has an average yield of 2.9 percent," he said.

The sale of France Telecom shares will start with a three-week reservation period for French retail investors on May 6, during which they can indicate how many shares they want to buy, without an obligation to take the shares after the final price has been set on May 26.
The IPO proper will start on May 27 and close on June 3 with first trading in Paris and New York scheduled for June 9.
